newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU fires second salvo on environment rules.
newsitem.headline: EU fires second salvo on environment rules.

text.p: The European Commission stepped up efforts to enforce the bloc's environmental rules on Tuesday, firing its second salvo in two days of court actions against EU countries.

"This shows two things. First of all, that there are still too many infringements (of environmental rules) and secondly, that the Commission has the will to act," Commission spokesman Peter Jorgensen told a news briefing.

Jorgensen said the Commission's new get-tough policy of court action and fines had already brought successes against errant EU countries earlier this year, forcing them to comply with a variety of rules agreed by their environment ministers.
"There is no reason why the Commission should not increase the use of financial penalties... they seem to work very well."

Four separate statements on Tuesday followed Monday's action against eight EU countries over implementation of environmental rules intended to protect water quality, govern waste treatment and provide pollution data to the public.

On Tuesday, the Commission took Germany, Luxembourg, Portugal and Spain to the European Court of Justice for what it said was their failure to adopt and report to the Commission on national laws related to genetically modified organisms.
A separate action, on noise emitted by earth-moving machinery, involved court challenges to Italy and Belgium, and a final pre-court warning for France.
The third, targeting Austria and Portugal for court action, dealt with those two countries' alleged failure to comply with EU rules intended to cut various forms of air pollution.
Portugal was also the target of a Commission court challenge announced in the fourth statement, for its alleged failure to adopt EU laws intended to protect animals used in experiments.
The Commission also issued final warnings to Spain and Italy related to implementation of wildlife protection laws and environmental impact assessment rules respectively.
